chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from Yahya al-Halabi from Harun ibn Harizah from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed tawaf around the House with eight paces (shawat) of the obligatory [seven], he said: 'He must repeat it until he completes it.'

And this report does not contradict what has been narrated regarding that he adds six paces to it, because those reports are applied to one who forgot and performed eight paces, for it is permissible for him to add six others to it, then he prays four raka'at.
As for doing it deliberately, it is obligatory upon him to repeat, according to what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs tawaf with eight paces instead of seven?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the distinction between deliberate error and forgetfulness in tawaf, ruling that intentional omission of a shaw requires full repetition, whereas forgetfulness allows for completion by adding a single shaw followed by two rak'at. This nuance highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of differentiating between *al-ikhtiyar* (choice) and *al-nas* (forgetfulness) in ritual validity. The hadith thus serves as a key reference for understanding the flexibility within the strict requirements of Hajj rituals.
